title: eRTMAC-NWIS (Nearby Wells Intelligence System): An AI-Powered Offset Well Knowledge and Decision Support Platform for Drilling Operations
description:
• Background Oil India Limited has a digital real-time monitoring system (eRTMAC) that provides real-time drilling data, mud logging information, and wellsite analytics across operational areas. However, drilling decisions, particularly in geologically complex formations, require not only real-time data from the active well but also insights from nearby and historical wells drilled in the same reservoir or formation. Historical drilling knowledge currently resides across numerous well completion reports, drilling reports, PDF documents, and individual experience, making retrieval time-consuming and dependent on individual experience &
memory. This often results in delays in decision-making and missed opportunities to proactively mitigate drilling risks.
• Problem Description Currently, drilling teams do not have a unified platform that can:
i. Display nearby wells on a geospatial map relative to the active well.
ii. Provide instant access to historical drilling experiences and operational events from offset wells.
iii. Correlate drilling parameters, reservoir characteristics, mud losses, kicks, stuck pipe incidents, casing programs, cementing practices, and formation-specific risks across wells.
iv. Generate proactive alerts when current drilling operations approach depths or formations where similar challenges were encountered in nearby wells.
As a result, engineers often spend significant time manually searching through historical reports and databases, limiting the ability to make fast, informed, and data-driven operational decisions.
• Expected Outcome / Solution Develop an AI/ML-enabled Nearby Wells Intelligence System (NWIS) that acts as a standalone decision-support platform alongside eRTMAC that has institutional memory.
The solution should:
i. Use AI, NLP, OCR, and data analytics to automatically extract and structure information from historical drilling reports and well documents.
ii. Provide an interactive map-based visualization of nearby wells within a user-defined radius.
iii. Create a searchable knowledge repository of drilling events, lessons learned, operational challenges, and mitigation measures.
iv. Correlate geological, drilling, and reservoir data across wells based on depth and formation.
v. Develop predictive analytics models that can identify potential drilling risks such as mud losses, stuck pipe, overpressure zones, torque spikes, or cementing issues based on historical offset-well behaviour.
vi. Generate real-time alerts and recommendations to assist drilling engineers in proactive decision-making.
vii. Present information through a user-friendly dashboard for field and office-based personnel.
• Relevant Data Availability (if any)
Potential data sources available within OIL may include:
i. Well Completion Reports (WCRs)
ii. Daily Drilling Reports (DDRs)
iii. Drilling and mud logging databases iv. Historical well parameters and drilling records v. Reservoir and geological data vi. eRTMAC data streams vii. Well trajectory and survey data viii. Casing, cementing, and mud program records ix. Historical operational event records including mud losses, kicks, stuck pipe incidents, fishing operations, and NPT events.
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, ml, nlp applied to a smart automation problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Smart Automation. Tech Depth (3/5): centers on real-time. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 18/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: eRTMAC-NWIS: AI-Powered Offset Well Knowledge and Decision Support Platform

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a system that shows drilling teams a map of nearby wells and instantly surfaces relevant historical drilling problems, mud losses, stuck pipe, kicks, from those wells' old reports, instead of relying on individual memory and manually digging through PDFs.
overview.why_it_matters: Drilling risk knowledge currently lives scattered across old reports and individual experience. Making that historical knowledge instantly accessible and geospatially relevant directly helps drilling teams avoid repeating known problems.
pain_points: Historical drilling knowledge is scattered across many completion/drilling reports and individual memory.
No unified platform shows nearby wells geospatially with linked historical insights.
Retrieval of relevant historical events (mud losses, kicks, stuck pipe) is slow and experience-dependent.
overview.background: Oil India's eRTMAC provides real-time drilling data, but historical offset-well knowledge (critical for geologically complex formations) remains scattered across documents, causing delays and missed risk-mitigation opportunities.
overview.whats_being_asked: An AI-powered platform displaying nearby wells geospatially, providing instant access to historical drilling events/reports, and correlating drilling parameters and formation-specific risks across offset wells.
expected_solution: Geospatial map showing nearby/offset wells relative to the active well.
Instant retrieval of historical drilling events from offset well reports (mud loss, kicks, stuck pipe).
Correlation of drilling parameters and formation-specific risks across wells.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: High. Combining geospatial well visualization with document-based historical-event retrieval (NLP over drilling reports) is a genuinely useful, technically substantial integration.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Moderate-high. Requires document extraction/NLP over technical drilling reports, geospatial visualization, and correlation logic together, real cross-domain effort.

competitive_landscape.note: Highly specialized oil-and-gas drilling-operations domain, requires genuine petroleum engineering context to build meaningfully.

innovation.note: Genuine geospatial-plus-document-retrieval integration specifically for drilling risk knowledge is a real, valuable, technically substantial application.

invention.note: Document extraction from technical drilling reports plus geospatial correlation is real, non-trivial engineering.

technical_feasibility.note: Real Oil India well/drilling report data isn't accessible; a realistic synthetic dataset with representative report content is the practical path.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly reduces drilling risk and decision-delay for a real, high-stakes industrial operation.

architecture.note: Document extraction/RAG plus geospatial visualization feeding a decision-support interface, well-understood pattern applied to a specialized domain.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team comfortable with document-based RAG and geospatial visualization. Real data isn't accessible, so ground your synthetic well/report dataset in realistic drilling terminology and event types.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Clear, well-specified functional requirements (geospatial display, historical event retrieval, correlation) give a concrete, demoable target.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Without realistic drilling-domain terminology and event types in your synthetic data, the historical-event-retrieval demo risks feeling generic rather than genuinely drilling-specific.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Research real drilling report terminology and common event types (mud loss, kick, stuck pipe, casing issues) to construct a genuinely realistic synthetic dataset of offset well reports.

idea_0_4: Research real drilling report structure and common event terminology to ground your synthetic dataset.
Construct a synthetic multi-well dataset with realistic geospatial positions and drilling event reports.
Split: one person on the geospatial map/visualization, one on the document extraction/retrieval logic.
prototype_4_22: Build your geospatial map showing offset wells relative to a simulated active well.
Build your document extraction/retrieval system for historical drilling events from your synthetic reports.
Start correlation logic linking active-well conditions to relevant offset-well historical events.
integration_22_30: Connect the map, retrieval, and correlation into one coherent decision-support interface.
Test with a realistic scenario, an active well approaching a formation depth where an offset well historically had a kick or stuck pipe event.
Add basic real-time data integration simulation (representing eRTMAC-style live drilling data).
polish_30_36: Polish the interface for genuine drilling-team usability.
Rehearse a live demo showing a relevant historical event surfacing proactively as the simulated active well approaches a risky depth.
Prepare to be honest about your synthetic data scope versus real Oil India well records.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show your system proactively surfacing a relevant historical offset-well event (e.g. a known stuck-pipe risk at a similar depth/formation) as your simulated active well approaches that condition, that proactive, context-aware retrieval is the actual value proposition beyond just a searchable document archive.

strengths: Clear, well-specified functional requirements give a concrete, demoable target.
Genuine operational value for a real, high-stakes drilling context.
weaknesses: Real Oil India data isn't accessible, synthetic realism in drilling terminology is the key credibility factor.
Requires genuine petroleum engineering domain context to build meaningfully.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Balanced, with real domain research into drilling terminology and event types.
team_fit.approach: Research real drilling report structure and terminology before constructing synthetic data.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: The document retrieval/RAG pipeline and geospatial mapping visualization.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Constructing genuinely realistic drilling event scenarios and terminology, and correctly correlating active-well conditions to relevant historical risks, that requires real petroleum engineering domain understanding.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: A system tested only against generic, non-drilling-specific synthetic content would not demonstrate genuine value for the actual, specialized drilling-risk-knowledge problem this PS addresses.

data_resource_availability.status: Real Oil India well/drilling report data isn't accessible to a hackathon team; a well-researched synthetic dataset is the practical path.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Construct a synthetic dataset grounded in real drilling report terminology and common event types, clearly labeled as illustrative.

judge_qna.question: How realistic is your synthetic drilling report data compared to actual well completion/drilling reports?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Describe the real drilling terminology and event types you researched and incorporated, not generic or invented content.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the biggest real-world drilling report format complexity your synthetic data might not capture?

judge_qna.question: How does your correlation logic decide which historical events are actually relevant to the current active well?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through your specific correlation criteria, formation type, depth proximity, geological similarity, not just raw geographic distance.
judge_qna.follow_up: What happens when multiple offset wells have conflicting historical experiences at a similar depth/formation?
